questions.q: Why are patient_name, appointment_type, clinic_location, and scheduling_notes the fields chosen for auditing on Meridian's Patient Scheduling record, rather than every field?
options: They're the patient-adjacent fields a HIPAA review would actually ask about, applying Lesson 19's selective-auditing principle instead of auditing everything
They were chosen at random to demonstrate that auditing is turned on somewhere in the instance
They are the only fields ServiceNow technically allows to be audited
They are the fields with the lowest storage cost, which was the sole deciding factor
questions.explain: Selective auditing targets fields that genuinely carry compliance or risk weight — here, the patient-adjacent fields a HIPAA review would focus on — not every field indiscriminately.

questions.q: What does Meridian's security_admin elevation policy require beyond simply logging that an elevation happened?
options: A logged justification naming the intended ACL change, plus an active manager notification, plus a post-hoc review comparing the justification to the actual edit made
Nothing further — logging the elevation event alone is sufficient under this policy
A requirement that security_admin never be used under any circumstances
Automatic reversal of any ACL edit made during an elevated session
questions.explain: The policy closes the gap Lesson 18 warned about: logging alone can go unreviewed, so it adds manager notification and a comparison of the justification against the actual change made.

questions.q: In the governance package's responsibility split, which item is listed as something Meridian's own team owns, not something the platform provides?
options: Choosing which specific fields are patient-adjacent and need auditing
The existence of the sys_audit field-level logging mechanism itself
The existence of the Elevate Roles / security_admin mechanism itself
The existence of encryption and masking capabilities on the platform
questions.explain: The platform provides the mechanisms (audit logging, ACLs, elevation, encryption); deciding which specific fields and roles those mechanisms apply to is Meridian's own responsibility.

questions.q: When leadership asks 'are we HIPAA compliant now?', what is the honest answer this lesson models?
options: A direct yes, framed around the platform mechanisms configured, but naming that full HIPAA compliance also depends on things outside ServiceNow entirely, like staff training and incident response
A flat 'yes, ServiceNow certifies this automatically'
A flat 'no, ServiceNow cannot support any HIPAA-relevant work'
A refusal to answer, since compliance questions are never answerable by anyone on the implementation team
questions.explain: The honest answer names what's been configured on the platform specifically, while being explicit that full compliance depends on things this governance package doesn't and can't cover.

questions.q: What does the governance package's audited-field list (the explicit 'audited' vs. 'not audited' breakdown) actually prove to a reviewer?
options: That auditing was a deliberate, scoped decision based on which fields carry compliance weight, not an unexamined assumption that everything is already logged
That every field in the instance, without exception, is being audited
That ServiceNow's default configuration already satisfies HIPAA with no further action needed
That Meridian's team never needs to review this list again once it's written
questions.explain: A named list of what's audited and what isn't, with reasoning, is the actual evidence a reviewer wants — proof the decision was deliberate, not a blanket assumption.
